new_arm_drift_exposure: aws_run.sh fetches `main` on the instance at BOOT, so the tree measured is main-as-of-~15:13Z, which may be 1-2 commits past the ffeb0aa recorded here. NOT pinned to a SHA, because the `origin/` prefix defeats SHA pinning on this path (same root cause as above). REGISTERED AS AN EXPOSURE, judged immaterial: the contrast spans hundreds of commits, so a 1-2 commit drift on the new arm cannot change the sign of the reading. It WOULD matter for an arm wave; it does not matter for a yardstick.

market_deviation_from_GH158.arithmetic: aws_run.sh syncs to S3 exactly ONCE, after BOTH directions finish (`aws s3 sync $OUT s3://...` is the second-to-last line of the user-data). There is no per-game upload. So on this path a reclaim is a TOTAL LOSS with nothing recoverable -- recover_verdict.py saved W42 precisely because soak_loop uploads per game, and that safety net DOES NOT EXIST here. W47 lost 2 of 4 machines to capacity; W43 lost 4 of 4. Immunity costs ~$0.42 (on-demand $0.673/h vs spot $0.231-0.250/h for ~1h). The owner priority this wave serves has already slipped two rounds; another total loss costs a further 3h round, and this path cannot recover partial data.

harvest_instructions.layout: fwd: Radiant=NEW(main), Dire=OLD(upstream). rev (--swap): Radiant=OLD, Dire=NEW. Half the games each way -- that is this path's side-bias cancellation.
harvest_instructions.fields: tools/batch_test/parse_log.py emits `winner` ('radiant'|'dire'), `duration_s`, and per-player {team, gpm, ...}. Everything P4.1 asks for (win rate + gpm delta + game count) is computable from these.
harvest_instructions.method: compute NEW-side minus OLD-side per game, then average the fwd stratum and the rev stratum SEPARATELY and take the arithmetic mean of the two strata. Iron rule 4(i-a): register BOTH strata's READINGS, not their game counts. Iron rule 4(i-d): NEVER weight the pooled number by game count.
harvest_instructions.winrate: this is the one channel that is NOT degenerate by construction here: the arms are different TREES, so a side sweep does not force 0.500 the way it does in the mirrored path. Census the winner side anyway and report the minority-side share before citing it.
harvest_instructions.if_empty: an empty prefix means the run died before its single terminal sync -- that is a TOTAL LOSS, not a zero reading, and must not be written up as 'measured, no effect'.

root_causes: PermissionError [Errno 13] on /opt/ab_fwd and /opt/ab_rev: the user-data runs make_ab_build.py as `sudo -u ubuntu` but /opt is root-owned, so ubuntu cannot create the output dir

sudo: steamcmd: command not found -- non-fatal (guarded by || true); the AMI's existing Dota install was fine (run_batch.sh's [ -x $DOTA_BIN ] check passed)
attempt_1_FAILED.FOURTH_FINDING_THE_DANGEROUS_ONE: run_batch.sh, handed NO bots directory at all, prints one line -- 'WARNING: ... bots will be default AI' -- and then plays the games anyway. Had /opt/results happened to be writable, this run would have played 80 games of DEFAULT AI vs DEFAULT AI and uploaded them as the upstream yardstick. A failure that looks exactly like data. It did not happen here for one reason only: the second bug blocked it. Root cause lives in run_batch.sh (another seat's instrument) -- handed to the director, not fixed here.
attempt_1_FAILED.WHAT_IT_BOUGHT: for ~$0.03, the log proves the ref resolution leg is HEALTHY: `--old origin/upstream-baseline --new origin/main` was accepted, git fetch and pull both succeeded. So GH #33's 'the baseline needs a tag first' is confirmed OBSOLETE by measurement, not by argument.
